title: Make a seat change all or nothing

blocks.text: The airline's app lets passengers change seats after check-in. Support has three kinds of tickets about it. Some passengers who picked a seat number from an old seat plan, one this aircraft doesn't have, were left with no seat at all. Twice, two passengers ended up holding the same seat, after one of them picked a seat that showed as free on a page loaded a minute earlier. And one passenger "moved" out of a seat that belonged to someone else.

Write `rebook(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/SeatMap.java`. When you're done, a seat change either happens completely or is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message names the seat at fault, and a refused request leaves every seat exactly as it was. About ten lines.
`assign(...)`, which check-in uses, is already written.

cases.says: a passenger moves from the seat they hold to a free seat, and the old seat becomes free
a passenger can change seats several times in a row
a target seat that isn't on the flight is refused before the passenger's current seat is freed
a target seat held by another passenger is refused, and nobody loses a seat
a passenger can't move out of a seat someone else holds

origin.section: Throw Where the Bad Value Arrives, Before Anything Changes

concepts: A method checks its arguments and preconditions before its first change of state, so a refused request leaves nothing half done.
A bad value that nothing checks may not fail at all; a negative amount runs a transfer backwards.
